study_identification.title: Heterogeneity of morphometric similarity networks in health and schizophrenia

study_characteristics.study_objective: This study assessed regional morphometric similarity as an indicator of cortical inter-regional connectivity, employing longitudinal normative modeling to evaluate whether decreases are consistent across individuals with schizophrenia.

dataset_name.answer: aomic (id1000, piop1, piop2), camcan, dlbs, ixi, narratives, oasis3, rockland, sald, Utrecht Schizophrenia project, Genetic Risk and Outcome of Psychosis (GROUP) consortium

hc_age.answer: See Fig. 1 for age distribution of each dataset. Clinical healthy controls: mean 30.44, sd 11.02 at baseline.

hc_sex.answer: See Fig. 1 for sex distribution of each dataset. Clinical healthy controls: F 130 (44.5%).

quality_checking_detail.answer: The Freesurfer Euler number was extracted as a proxy for image quality. Subjects were removed if the maximum, absolute, within-dataset centered Euler number was larger than 10, and 29 subjects were removed. For the clinical sample, extensive visual and non-visual image quality control procedures were applied, including signal-to-noise ratio, contrast-to-noise ratio, Foreground to background Energy Ratio, percent artifact Voxels, and Entropy Focus Criterion. Outliers were defined as [mean - (2.698 × SD)].

site_effect_handling_detail.answer: Bayesian linear regression (BLR) with likelihood warping was used to predict morphometric similarity from a vector of covariates (age, sex, Euler number, and scanner).

modeling_method.answer: Bayesian linear regression (BLR) with likelihood warping

software_tool.answer: caret R package, and code available at https://github.com/iamjoostjanssen/NormModel_MorphoSim_SZ

predictor_effects.answer: Not specified as fixed or random effects, but covariates in a Bayesian linear regression model.

nm_vldtn_handle_ns.reason: The model included scanner and Euler number as covariates to handle site and image quality effects.
nm_vldtn_handle_ns.supporting_text: Bayesian linear regression (BLR) with likelihood warping using a B-spline (spline order = 3, number of knots = 5) was used to predict morphometric similarity from a vector of covariates (age, sex, Euler number, and scanner).

nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.reason: The model was evaluated on a held-out test set.
nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.supporting_text: The unseen data in the complete test set was used to evaluate the normative model.

nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.reason: The model was evaluated on a test set (≈10% of healthy controls from 10 datasets, and 80% of healthy controls from the clinical dataset).
nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.supporting_text: For normative modeling, each of the ten datasets containing only healthy controls was split into a training set ( ≈ 90%) and a test set ( ≈ 10%)... For the clinical dataset, all individuals with schizophrenia, as well as 80% of the healthy controls, were included in the test set, while the remaining healthy controls (20%) were included in the training set.

nm_vldtn_diff_domain.reason: The validation was performed on a split of the same datasets used for training.
nm_vldtn_diff_domain.supporting_text: Eleven datasets were combined to create the full sample...For normative modeling, each of the ten datasets containing only healthy controls was split into a training set ( ≈ 90%) and a test set ( ≈ 10%).

clinical_dataset.answer: Utrecht Schizophrenia project and the Genetic Risk and Outcome of Psychosis (GROUP) consortium

deviation_metric.answer: z-score. z-score ≧ 1.96 as supra-normal and a z-score ≦ -1.96 as infra-normal.

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: Welch t-tests to compare z-scores between groups. Pearson correlation to test for associations between z-scores and IQ and PANSS scores.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: Individuals with schizophrenia exhibited decreased morphometric similarity in the default mode network, but these abnormalities were not progressive over time and were present only in a minority of individuals.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: At baseline, individuals with schizophrenia showed increased morphometric similarity in the somatomotor network (d=0.30, p<0.01) and decreased morphometric similarity in the DMN (d=-0.36, p<0.001) compared to controls. The percentage of individuals with extreme deviations was low (<6%) in both groups. Longitudinally, there were no significant differences in the change of z-scores over time between groups.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: The training set, while substantial, could be larger and more diverse (not solely European ancestry). The model treats each region independently, ignoring potential correlations. The normative model can only detect deviations, not condition-specific biomarkers. The sample size of individuals with schizophrenia was relatively small for a longitudinal study.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: The study is the first to apply normative modeling to morphometric similarity in a longitudinal sample of individuals with schizophrenia. It provides a layout for future studies using normative modeling with cross-sectional and longitudinal neuroimaging phenotypes.

general_notes.general_notes: The study found that normative modeling may possess the capacity to capture overarching population patterns, discern clinical disparities between groups, and retain the ability to investigate individual differences, showing increased statistical significance compared to raw data models.
